summary: Backend-only verification of the Stripe TEST→LIVE key swap. 12/12 pytest cases pass (100%). Confirmed: (1) POST /api/billing/checkout plan=monthly returns 200 with a cs_live_ session_id and a Stripe-hosted URL on checkout.stripe.com (actual path observed is /f/pay/cs_live_... which is a valid Stripe hosted-checkout variant alongside /c/pay/ and /g/pay/; test accepts any path on checkout.stripe.com that contains cs_live_ and does NOT contain cs_test_). (2) plan=yearly returns 200 with a distinct cs_live_ session, URL contains cs_live_. (3) Session retrieved via Stripe SDK confirms livemode=True, billing_address_collection='auto', mode='subscription', metadata.{device_id,user_id,plan} preserved, client_reference_id==device_id, allow_promotion_codes=true, and the line_item price has livemode=True — so the LIVE price IDs are being used. (4) Backend startup logs confirm _PRICE_IDS populated with LIVE IDs: monthly=price_1URhgTIBA9UCVOAfjJI3qwZV, yearly=price_1URhgTIBA9UCVOAfh0twDzAC under new live product prod_VScwaFGOyi5S5L (different from the previous test-mode IDs prod_VScCaetY3ciCd3 / price_1URgxfIBA9UCVOAf*). (5) Full regression — /api/analyze (text), /api/transcribe multipart, /api/history POST+GET with X-Device-Id, /api/auth/apple + /api/auth/google invalid tokens → 4xx, /api/billing/status unknown device → 'inactive', /api/billing/verify bogus session_id → 404 — all pass. NO regressions from the key swap. Important note: tests only CREATE Checkout Sessions — they never complete payment, so no real money was charged.
critical_code_review_comments: billing.py handles live-mode seamlessly — ensure_products() ran against the live account at startup and created a fresh 'NarcCheck Pro' product + monthly ($8.99) + yearly ($60) recurring prices. The idempotent find-or-create logic correctly avoided duplicates on subsequent restarts.

STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is still empty in backend/.env (line 8). For PRODUCTION live mode, this MUST be set to a whsec_... from the Stripe Dashboard webhook endpoint so subscription.updated/deleted and invoice.payment_failed events are signature-verified. The current webhook handler accepts unsigned payloads when the secret is empty — safe only for dev. Flagging as a hardening item for main agent before public launch (not blocking checkout flow, but critical for cancellation + renewal tracking in production).
